result.title: Mesh-Agnostic Refinement Models for Latent Space Encoding of 3D Human Body Shapes
result.summary: Parametric human body models such as the Skinned Multi-Person Linear (SMPL) model provide compact representations of human shape and pose, but their reconstructions remain affected by both errors in estimated latent parameters and limitations in the decoder's expressive capacity. We propose a framework for refining these reconstructions by exploiting the geometric discrepancy between an initial decoded surface and a target mesh, without requiring vertex correspondences between them. The framework comprises three complementary approaches. Latent-VaRefine uses varifold-distance gradients to correct the estimated latent code while preserving the original parametric representation. Vertex-VaRefine processes multiscale varifold-gradient features with a DiffusionNet backbone to predict vertex displacements in a canonical pose, yielding an approximately pose-equivariant refinement pipeline. ElaOpt directly optimizes surface deformations under elastic regularization and normal-direction constraints.

AI.brief_summary: 提出面向 SMPL 人体形状重建的网格无关精化框架：利用初始解码表面与目标网格的几何差异，在无需顶点对应的情况下分别用 varifold 距离梯度修正 latent code、用 DiffusionNet 预测顶点位移，或以弹性正则直接优化形变。
AI.relevance_reason: 「用目标几何证据的梯度反修 latent 码」这一状态更新线索可能与 LVR 中 latent 表示的精化与证据筛选相关，但领域为 3D 人体几何，与视觉推理的关系需核查其梯度信号是否可迁移。
